main_text.p: rationem habet rugæ cutis: ut in senibus, gra cilibus & recens iudicatis. Sæpius etiam hu miditates, & præsertim si ipsa arteriarum cor pora, his diluta fuerint, ut in hyderis.

p.i: Arteriæ distensio in magnitudinem coarctata, locis arteriæ circumiectis, tumorem hunc non capientibus.

main_text.p: Longū, latū, & altū primæ tabellæ pulsus:

p.i: Gracilitas aduentitia, si tanta, quanto pul-sus est maior.
Calor solus, si eadem habitudine fuerit cor-pus.
Calor duplo auctus, si corpus crassius euase-rit.
Notæ superiores, & cutis arteriæ summè in-cumbentis rugositas: perinde atq; membrum peruertas, ut pars superior inferior sit.
Superiores notæ, arteria mole obiectorū cor-porum valde onerata, imbecillior vna facul-tas, & summè mollis arteria.

page.notes: Printed text is in a mix of roman and italic type; the Latin rendering of long s has been normalised to s. Some words at line ends are hyphenated in the print (gra-cilibus, pul-sus, cor-pus, euase-rit, in-cumbentis, facul-tas) and are kept as printed. The last word "Longum," at the foot is a catchword-like line and is treated as text.
